en: The Great Cloud Sūtra, Chapter Sixty-four: Invoking Rain.
Translated during the Zhou dynasty by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānayaśas.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was dwelling in the palace of the Nāga Kings Nanda and Upananda.
Within the precious pavilion of the Maṇicūḍa Great Cloud Wheel Treasury,
he was together with a great assembly of bhikṣus, great bodhisattvas,
and all the great nāgas, including the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda.
The nāga king Sāgara, the nāga king Anavatapta,
the nāga king Manasvin, the nāga king Vāsuki,
the nāga king Takṣaka, and the nāga king Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
The Naga King Vasuki, the Naga King Mucilinda,
the Naga King Elapatra, the Naga King Bhadra,
the Naga King Tejasvin, and the Naga King Gunabhadra.
The Naga King Vidyut-mālā, the Naga King Mahā-jaṭa,
the Naga King Maṇi-jaṭa, the Naga King Prabhāsa-piṅgala,
the Naga King Indra-śastra-śūla-khaḍga, and the Naga King Indra-dhvaja.
The Naga King Indrāyudha, the Naga King Jambūnada-dhvaja,
the Naga King Kṣema, the Naga King Mahācakra,
the Naga King Mahoraga, and the Naga King Agnijihva.
The Dragon King Candraprabha, the Dragon King Śrīmanta,
the Dragon King Sulocana, and the Dragon King Atisulocana.
The Dragon King Well-Abiding, the Dragon King Jewel-Neck,
the Dragon King Born from Clouds, the Dragon King Holding Rain,
the Dragon King Exerting Power, and the Dragon King Exerting Power Left and Right.
The Dragon King Vighuṣṭaśabda, the Dragon King Mahāpiṇḍa,
the Dragon King Mahāgrīva, the Dragon King Gambhīraśabda,
the Dragon King Mahānāda, and the Dragon King Vinālitīrtha.
The Utpala Dragon King, the Mahāvihāra Dragon King,
the Varṣadhara Dragon King, the Citrasena Dragon King,
the Mahāpāśa Dragon King, and the Elāpattra Dragon King.
First, he offered greetings and inquiries after the welfare of King Dragon Aśvalakarṇa,
King Dragon Śaṅkha, King Dragon Dādhara,
King Dragon Upadādhara, and King Dragon Mahāśvasta.
The Dragon King Prahlāda, the Dragon King Mahāprahlāda,
the Dragon King Mahābala, the Dragon King Huluhula,
the Dragon King Aparāla, and the Dragon King Lambuka.
The Nāga King Kṛtaka, the Nāga King Kāla,
the Nāga King Indrasena, the Nāga King Nata,
the Nāga King Upanata, and the Nāga King Gambuḥrina.
The Dragon King Bhadrapāliṇa, the most handsome Dragon King,
the Dragon King Gajabhuja, the Dragon King Kṛpāṇa,
the Yellow Dragon King, and the Dragon King Vidyutprabha.
The Naga King Great Lightning Flash,
the Naga King Celestial Power, the Naga King Kambala,
the Naga King Balāha, the Naga King Amṛta, and the Naga King Tīrthakīna.
The Naga King Vaidūryaprabha, the Naga King Suvarṇakeśa,
the Naga King Suvarṇaprabha, the Naga King Candradhvajaprabha,
the Naga King Sūryaprabha, and the Naga King Udayana.
The Ox-Head Nāga King, the White Nāga King,
the Black Nāga King, the Yama Nāga King,
the Śamandī Nāga King, and the Frog Nāga King.
The Nāga King Saṃghāṭa, the Nāga King Nimindhara,
the Nāga King Mahīdhara, the Thousand-headed Nāga King,
the Nāga King Ratnaśikhin, and the Nāga King Amoghadarśin.
The Nāga King Megha, the Nāga King Suvarṇa,
the Nāga King Govinda, the Nāga King Manuṣyadeva,
the Nāga King Vinīta, and the Nāga King Jarāya.
The Naga King Kumbhīra, the Naga King Mukhakumbhīra,
the Naga King Vinatara, the Naga King Aśvīśana,
the Naga King Padma, and the Naga King Dīrghapuccha.
The nāga king Pārāmaṇi, the nāga king Bhayadatta,
the nāga king Suśrī, the five-headed nāga king,
the nāga king Bala, and the nāga king Jaratana.
The Dragon King Shangwei, the Great-Head Dragon King,
the Binbiji Dragon King, the Bicā Dragon King,
the Horse Dragon King, and the Three-Headed Dragon King.
The dragon king Nāgasena, the dragon king Mahātejas,
the dragon king Naradatta, the dragon king Vemacitra,
the dragon king Prabhāsa, and the seven-headed dragon king.
The Dragon King Mahādruma, the Dragon King Priyadarśana,
the Dragon King Mahāpāpa, the Dragon King Vimalatejas,
the Dragon King Sudarśana, and the Dragon King Mahāgaurīṇa.
The Dragon King Jvālāskandha, the Dragon King Mahācaṇḍa,
the Dragon King Mahāroṣaṇa, the Dragon King Ratnamegha,
the Dragon King Mahāmeghavāripradāna, and the Dragon King Indraprabha.
The Naga King Tree, the Naga King Cloud-Moon,
the Naga King Ocean-Cloud, the Naga King Great Fragrance Kumuda,
the Naga King Kumuda-Khara, and the Naga King Jewel-Eye.
The Nāga King Mahāmahiṣadhvaja, the Nāga King Mahāmeghagarbha,
the Nāga King Himavat, the Nāga King Guṇagañja,
the Nāga King Meghaśūla, and the Nāga King Haraṣavindala.
The Dragon King Cloud-Dragon, the Dragon King Great-Cloud-Water-Emergence,
the Dragon King Great-Cloud-Great-Water-Emergence, the Dragon King Great-Fire-Majesty,
the Dragon King Great-Cloud-Wealth, and the Dragon King Free-from-Anger.
The Nāga King Kuku, the Nāga King Vīrabala,
the Nāga King Sāgara, the Nāga King Meghola,
the Nāga King Indraka, and the Nāga King Tejasvin.
The Nāga King of Izumo, the Nāga King of Immeasurable Conduct,
the Nāga King Sucana, the Nāga King Mahākāya,
the Nāga King Mahodara, and the Nāga King Kṣema.
The Dragon King Vīrya, the Dragon King Kālakūṭa,
the Dragon King Utpala, the Dragon King Viśvakiṇa, the Dragon King Susvara,
and the Dragon King Amṛtadṛḍha who pours down great rain.
The nāga kings Vīkṣuṇi-ti, who produces sound by clashing together;
the nāga king Drumasvararāja; the nāga king Amṛtasaṃpāta;
the nāga king Nandika; and the nāga king Stanitaghosha.
The Dragon King Vīrabala, the Dragon King Nārāyaṇa,
the Dragon King Bhadrapāla, the Dragon King Vikarṇa,
and all such great dragon kings as these were the leaders.
Together with eighty-four billion hundred thousand nayutas of nāga kings, they were seated in the assembly.
At that time, those nāga kings, along with their retinues,
rose from their seats and bared their right shoulders.
Kneeling with his right knee on the ground and joining his palms toward the Buddha,
he offered immeasurable, incalculable, and various kinds of most excellent,
sublime incense, flowers, unguents, powdered incense, and burning incense.
As well as various flower garlands, diverse garments, banners, streamers, and silken fabrics;
music, songs, precious flowers, and jeweled canopies;
assorted pendants, tassels, and hanging necklaces.
With dragon-flower pearl nets and an extensive array of offerings,
they made offerings to the Tathāgata with great steadfastness,
reverence, and respect, and with inconceivable, supreme, pure, and profound faith.
Having made this offering and circumambulated the Buddha to the right, they stood to one side.
Simultaneously raising their voices, they uttered this great vow:
"May we, with bodies as vast as oceans, equal in number to every single atom within the atoms of all worlds, [serve as offerings]."
The ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
the ocean of all worlds, which is incalculable;
and the ocean of all atoms of earth, water, fire, and wind of the four great elements.
All the light-radiance of forms, like motes of dust, within each and every mote, surpasses oceans of calculation;
they are immeasurable, incalculable *asaṃkhyeya*, inconceivable, and beyond all description or expression—such are the oceans of bodies.
Within each and every body, with immeasurable hands—
countless as oceanic clouds—
they manifested various kinds of offering implements.
In every single atom throughout the ten directions, may they remain neither interrupted nor dispersed, like oceans of clouds. Furthermore,
I vow that we shall always, in every place, offer all manner of worship to the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
All that is immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, and inexpressible— uninterrupted and undispersed— is,
throughout all ten directions, like the ocean-clouds of the physical bodies of the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
By the power of their mental vows, they universally pervade the empty space of the ten directions;
thus they accomplish the bodies of Bodhisattvas, which are like oceans of clouds.
At that time, there appear oceans of clouds of the solar and lunar wheels of all jewel-colored light-flames, which are neither interrupted nor dispersed.
Ocean-clouds of all kinds of jeweled canopies with hanging tassels and multitudes of flower-groves;
ocean-clouds of all kinds of jeweled canopies that are great luminous treasuries of pavilions;
and ocean-clouds of caskets and treasuries from the branches of all trees.
Ocean-clouds manifesting all fragrances and colors;
ocean-clouds of all kinds of musical instruments with wondrous sounds and every form of speech;
and ocean-clouds of all fragrant trees.
Pervading the void, established by majestic spiritual power—
such immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya, inconceivable, and ineffable oceans of clouds, neither dispersing nor ceasing.
He makes offerings to the ocean of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
throughout the bounds of the future, he reveres, respects, prostrates to,
and provides for them with such offerings as the treasury of the mani-jewel of the realm of all great adornments.
Like flashes of lightning amidst oceanic clouds,
they are established by majestic spiritual power, filling the entirety of space.
Furthermore, may the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas likewise be so.
For as long as the limits of the future endure, they shall reverently honor, respect, prostrate to, and provide for them with such offerings as these:
clouds of oceans of mani-jewel kings adorned by rains of jewels that universally illuminate all.
Clouds of mani jewel ocean kings with the constant, unceasing emanation of the Buddha’s voice of all-jewel-flame illumination;
clouds of mani jewel ocean kings with the voice of universal delight in all Buddha-dharmas.
Throughout the ten directions, there appeared clouds of oceans of transformation-light rays from the Jewel-Flame Buddhas;
all manner of adornments, indestructible and undispersed, were entirely reflected therein as clouds of oceans of jewel-king flame-lamps.
Clouds of mani jewel oceans conforming to the spheres of all buddhas;
clouds of mani jewel oceans in which all inconceivable buddha-fields and the abodes of all Tathāgatas are reflected.
In this manner, I make offerings to all the various jewel-dust clouds of the bodies and reflections of the Buddhas of the three times, as well as to the Vairocana-maṇi-rāja ocean-clouds.
Having manifested this, which was established through majestic spiritual power filling all of space,
it was like a great ocean amidst the sea-like clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Until the end of the future, I shall reverently honor, respect, prostrate to, and provide for [the Buddhas].
May such offerings be made without distraction or interruption.
Furthermore, I vow that there shall be oceans of clouds of all kinds of precious incense, various flowers, and celestial palaces.
Ocean-clouds of pavilions adorned with all kinds of mani-jewel kings of immeasurable colors;
ocean-clouds of pavilions with jewel lamps and fragrant flames;
ocean-clouds of pavilions made of all varieties of pearls.
Having thus established clouds of oceans of all kinds of flower garlands and clouds of oceans of towers adorned with immeasurable multitudes of precious ornaments, necklaces,
and tassels, filling the entirety of space;
Infinite oceans of clouds of pavilions from the ten directions, formed through the harmonious transformation of all adornments of the Universal Blazing Fire Treasury;
and infinite oceans of clouds of pavilions from the ten directions, manifesting the adornments of all jewel flutes and jewel wheels.
Universal clouds-seas of all manner of ornamental carvings and decorations pervade the towers;
universal clouds-seas of flying pavilions, balustrades, bell-nets, canopies, and curtains fill the gates of the ten directions throughout space,
established by majestic spiritual power and fully manifested.
Toward all the oceans of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
until the end of the future, I shall pay respect, honor, prostrate, and provide offerings in this manner. Furthermore,
I vow to offer oceans of clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of joy, adorned with necklaces of various threads of gold, jewels, and pearls.
The ocean-cloud of lion thrones of various treasuries of floral radiance;
the ocean-cloud of lion thrones of various treasuries of *indranīla* and Jambu-river lotuses;
the ocean-cloud of lion thrones of the lotus-treasury of mani-lamps.
Ocean-clouds of lion-thrones with various treasuries of lotuses and flaming-jewel banners;
ocean-clouds of lion-thrones with various treasuries of jewel-adorned lotuses;
ocean-clouds of lion-thrones with lotus-treasury cores of exquisite, beautiful light-flames and Indra-blue color.
Ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the Lotus Treasury, blazing with the majestic power of inexhaustible light;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the Lotus Treasury, emitting all manner of jewel flames.
Having established through his majestic spiritual power an ocean-like cloud of lion thrones made of jewel-flames that produce all wondrous sounds from the Buddha’s lotus-womb,
which are neither interrupted nor dispersed and fill the entirety of space;
May they continue to offer such worship— reverently honoring, respecting, prostrating to, and providing for them— throughout the limits of the future. Furthermore,
may they vow to manifest ocean-like clouds of all kinds of precious incense and variegated trees,
wherein every leaf throughout the gates of the ten directions is like a joined palm, and these fragrant clouds form vast oceans of mist.
Ocean-clouds of manifestations of infinite adornments of the colors of all trees;
ocean-clouds of flower clouds draped and spread between all the trees;
and ocean-clouds of boundless caskets emerging from the adornments of all the trees.
The flaming garlands of all the jewel trees shine like ocean-clouds,
and from every branch of the sandalwood trees, there appear ocean-clouds of Bodhisattvas, each manifesting half their bodies.
The inconceivable adornment of the radiating light from the supreme wheel-light trees of all bodhisattvas, and the ocean-clouds of boundless jewel-garment caskets illuminated like the sun.
A sea-cloud of all trees universally emitting wondrous sounds that bring joy to those who hear them;
a sea-cloud of lion thrones with treasuries of exquisite lotuses made of boundless colored jewels;
and a sea-cloud of lion thrones with treasuries of the radiance of lightning from mani-jewel kings throughout the ten directions.
Ocean-clouds of lion thrones adorned with the carvings of various necklaces and treasuries;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of diverse jewel-flame lamp-garlands;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of universal sounds capable of emitting rains of jewels.
Ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of all fragrant flowers, garlands, and jewels;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of mani-kings that manifest the adornments of all Buddhas' seats.
Ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the wondrous treasuries of all kinds of ornaments, hanging tassels, curtains, canopies, and railings;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasuries of jewel caskets and boxes on the branches of all trees made of mani-jewels.
A network of various fragrant bells hung as curtains, spread everywhere like the radiance of the sun;
lion thrones like oceans of clouds filled the void without ceasing or dispersing.
Having performed these deeds, he—
Toward the ocean of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
one should offer such worship by revering, honoring, prostrating to, and providing for them.
Furthermore, one vows to offer oceans of clouds of canopies made of various sovereign wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels.
Ocean-clouds of canopies of jewel flower garlands adorned with Indra-blue ornaments;
ocean-clouds of canopies of all kinds of fragrant mani-jewels;
and ocean-clouds of canopies of lamp-light from bodies of jewel-flame colors.
Cloud-oceans of canopies of mani-kings that emit light and sound through the supernatural powers of all Buddhas;
cloud-oceans of canopies manifesting all adornments of various kinds of mani-jewels and precious garments emitting light.
Ocean-clouds of jeweled canopies emitting light from all manner of flowers;
ocean-clouds of netted canopies where the sounds of various bells universally resound;
and ocean-clouds of lotus-netted canopies with mani-jewel pedestals of boundless colors and variegated lotus lattices.
Oceans of clouds of canopies of golden garlands and flaming fire-banners;
inconceivable oceans of clouds of canopies of various necklaces with radiant light and shadows,
filling all of space without ceasing or dispersing.
Having established this,
one should respectfully revere, pay homage to, and provide offerings to all the oceans of clouds of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in this manner.
Furthermore, may I, with oceans of clouds of all kinds of mani-jewel canopies established in this manner, fill the entirety of space;
and [may I do so] with oceans of clouds of flower-canopies adorned with flames from the ten directions.
Ocean-clouds of canopies of infinite-colored pearl caskets;
ocean-clouds of canopies of mani-kings resounding with the gates of the great compassion of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
ocean-clouds of canopies of garlands of various miscellaneous jewel-flames.
Ocean-clouds of canopies and curtains of networks of bells adorned with universally beautiful jewel-fragrances;
ocean-clouds of canopies and curtains of all kinds of mani-jewel trees with hanging branches;
and sun-flame-illuminating mani-kings, burning incense and scattering incense.
Ocean-clouds of all kinds of incense canopies;
ocean-clouds of sandalwood powder incense, like caskets, universally shaking and pervasively covering;
ocean-clouds of the universally vast adornments and illuminations of the realms of all Buddhas, universally shaking and covering.
Without interruption or dispersion, they pay homage, show respect, prostrate, and provide offerings in this manner to all the oceans of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, they vow to do so with ocean-clouds of light-wheels made of every kind of jewel.
Cloud-oceans of light-circles shining incessantly from the bodies of various jewel-flames;
cloud-oceans of light-circles shining from clouds of flowers;
and cloud-oceans of light-circles manifested by all the jewel-flames of the Buddhas.
Ocean-clouds of light-wheel spheres manifesting the reflections of all buddha-fields;
ocean-clouds of jewel-branch light-wheel spheres capable of emitting thunderous sounds throughout the universal realm of all Buddhas;
and ocean-clouds of flaming light-wheel spheres of all Vaiḍūrya-jewel-natured maṇi-kings.
Cloud-seas of light-mandalas manifesting the forms and minds of infinite sentient beings in every instant;
cloud-seas of light-mandalas with voices that please all Buddhas;
and cloud-seas of light-mandalas of sovereign mani-jewel kings with voices from all assemblies and sites of enlightenment that teach and transform sentient beings.
Toward all the oceans of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
one should offer such worship by paying homage, showing respect, and making offerings with reverence;
furthermore, one vows to do so with clouds of oceans of flaming jewel caskets.
The ocean-clouds of the forms, sounds, fragrances, tastes, tangibles, and flames of all Buddhas;
the ocean-clouds of all jewel-flames;
and the ocean-clouds of the resounding flames from which the voices of all Buddha-dharmas emerge.
Ocean-clouds of radiant flames adorning all Buddha-fields;
ocean-clouds of floral flames from all celestial palaces;
ocean-clouds of radiant flames from all precious flutes.

In every single kalpa, throughout the succession of all kalpas, there are clouds of the ocean of blazing light from the Dharma-sounds of the Buddhas appearing in the world to teach and transform sentient beings;
and clouds of the ocean of blazing light from the manifestation of all flower garlands as inexhaustible, wondrous jewels for sentient beings.
They manifest oceans of clouds of light-flames that adorn all seats;
they continuously and uninterruptedly pay homage, show reverence, prostrate, and provide offerings in this manner to the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, may there be ocean-clouds of the radiant flames of infinite jewel-lights of unceasing and undispersed colors;
ocean-clouds of mani-jewel kings of universal radiance;
and ocean-clouds of the radiant flames that universally adorn and illuminate all Buddha-fields.
Clouds of oceans of flames of all fragrances;
clouds of oceans of flames of all adorned lights;
clouds of oceans of flames from the bodies of all manifested Buddhas.
Cloud-seas of the radiant flames of various jewel-trees and flower garlands;
cloud-seas of the radiant flames of all garments;
and cloud-seas of the radiant flames of the mani-jewel kings of the boundless conduct and renown of bodhisattvas.
Oceans of clouds of all pearl lamp-flames,
uninterrupted and undispersed throughout the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
like the great ocean.
They pay homage with reverence, respect, prostration, and offerings such as these.
Furthermore, they pray that there may arise inconceivable ocean-clouds of all kinds of incense, flowers, and various jewels;
and ocean-clouds of jewel-flame lotus flower nets.
Cloud-oceans of the light-wheels of the sovereign mani-jewel of boundless color;
cloud-oceans of caskets of pearls in all jewel colors;
cloud-oceans of powdered sandalwood incense of every precious fragrance.
Ocean-clouds of all kinds of jewel canopies;
ocean-clouds of mani-jewel kings with pure and wondrous sounds that delight the minds of all beings;
and ocean-clouds of necklaces and tassels consisting of sun-flame mani-luminous wheels.
Oceans of clouds of boundless jewel caskets;
oceans of clouds of the physical bodies of all Samantabhadras;
oceans of clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas that are neither interrupted nor dispersed.
Just as one would toward the great ocean,
they paid him honor, respect, prostrated, and made offerings in such a manner.
At that time, eighty-four billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of nāgas, having made this vow, [proceeded].
Having circumambulated the Buddha three times and prostrated with their heads at his feet, they stood to one side.
The Buddha said, "Sit down.
At that time, each of the nāgas sat down.
Within this great assembly was a great nāga king named Ānanda-parikarasa-gara-miga-ha-viyuha-kāti-vṛkṣa-maṇḍala-citra-rāja.
Among the lords of the nāgas in the trichiliocosm,
he dwells on the stage of non-retrogression;
by the power of his great vows, he has come to Jambudvīpa.
Desiring to make offerings to the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One,
and with a sincere heart to prostrate and listen to the True Dharma,
at that time Ānanda-tāpali-kasāgara-nāgarāja [acted].
Rising from his seat, he bared his right shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground,
and with palms joined toward the Buddha, paid homage with single-minded devotion.
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One."
"I now wish to ask the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, about a very minor matter.
If I am granted permission, I shall venture to ask.
When the World-Honored One heard these words, he [consented].
He addressed the Naga King Ānanda-tāpali-kasāgara, saying:
"Great King, ask whatever you wish;
if there is anything you desire to inquire about, now is the very time."
"I shall analyze and explain this for you so as to fulfill your aspiration.
At that time, the Dragon King addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how can all dragons be made to leave behind suffering and affliction and attain all forms of happiness?"
My wishes being thus fulfilled, this Jambudvīpa shall receive rain in its proper season;
the hundred grains, fruits, medicinal herbs, flowers, trees, and forests,
as well as all that grows from the soil, shall increase in their flavor.
"Because flavors increase, the people of Jambudvīpa obtain peace and happiness.
Having asked this question,
the Buddha addressed the great nāga king Sāgara, saying:
Excellent, excellent, O Dragon King!
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, you now inquire about such a matter.
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well.
I shall now speak.
Noble son, I possess a single dharma;
if all nāgas are able to receive and uphold it, [they shall be protected].
Thereby all sufferings are exhausted, and body and mind become peaceful and happy.
What is this one dharma?
It is what is called a compassionate heart.
Whether gods or humans, those who can practice and cultivate this cannot be burned by fire, cannot be wounded by blades,
cannot be swept away by water, and cannot be harmed by poisonous drugs.
Unable to be invaded by any internal or external thieves,
whether awake or asleep, one remains secure and tranquil,
being able to exercise self-restraint and protect one's own body through great merit and majestic virtue.
In life after life, they shall receive a handsome and upright body;
all who see them will love and delight in them, and wherever they go, they shall meet no obstacles.
No devas or humans shall be able to disturb or trouble them.
Free from all suffering and affliction, their minds are always joyful;
they experience various pleasures and attain the qualities of a superior person.
Should their lives come to an end, they will be reborn in the Brahma world.
Great Dragon King, in this way you benefit devas and humans with a compassionate heart;
you should constantly cultivate compassion in body, speech, and mind.
Furthermore, Great Dragon King, there is a dharani phrase.
It is named "Bestowing Peace and Bliss.
All these nāgas should constantly recite and uphold it;
it can eliminate all the suffering and afflictions of the nāgas.
It can cause all beings to be peaceful, secure, and happy.
Once they have attained such happiness,
those nāgas and others will, in accordance with the proper seasons, send down rain upon Jambudvīpa.
The hundred grains, fruits, medicinal herbs, flowers, trees, and forests all attain growth.
The Dragon King addressed the Buddha:
"What is called the dhāraṇī phrase for bestowing all happiness?"
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
*Tadyathā*. In this mantra, those characters with a small "mouth" (口) mark at their side are to be read with the tongue curled back;
those marked with a "note" (注) are to be read with a drawn-out, nasalized tone. *Dhāraṇi dhāraṇi eka...*
1. Tāriṇī 2. Parājitā 3. Vijayavāriṇī-satye parājita-jaya-dhana-vardhini 4.
Utpādani 5. Vināhani 6. Abhicchādanī 7. Abhibhūyiṣyati
Yehāra (8) Śūpahavati (9) Akimata (10) Jāṭi (11) Kuṃbhara (12) Pāṭipahā (13) Marakiliśadānapuḷaṇa (14)
Śūdaya-māṅga-nir-haka-dharmata (15) Śūda-ha-luka (16) Vidi-mi-ra-hara-ja-pada-kṣamaṇa (17) Sarva-buddha-ha-paruka-na-di-ś-citi (18) Pāra.
Jaya jayana pahi svāhā. The Buddha said:
"O Great Dragon King, this dhāraṇī..."
It is named "Bestowing Peace and Happiness upon All Nāgas.
These nāgas should constantly recite and uphold it;
they shall always obtain mastery over all necessities of life and enter the gate of sovereignty.
They are protected by the majestic spiritual power of all Tathāgatas,

The Rite for Rain.
Listen now attentively.
This master of the rain-invocation [is effective] for all sentient beings.
Arousing a heart of compassion, one should observe the eightfold precepts.
In an open, unsheltered space, one should set up a blue canopy and suspend ten blue banners.
One should thoroughly cleanse the ground and smear the site with cow dung.
Please have the mantra-reciter sit upon a green seat.
If he is a layperson, he should observe the eight precepts;
if he is a bhikṣu, he should maintain the prohibitive precepts.
All should wear pure garments and burn fine, renowned incense.
Furthermore, they should scatter powdered incense upon the Dharma Master’s seat and partake of three kinds of pure, white foods.
That is to say, using cow’s milk, curd, and non-glutinous rice,
one should sit facing east while reciting this "Great Cloud Wheel" chapter.
Day and night, with a sincere mind, one should maintain the sound without interruption.
Make offerings to all the Buddhas.
Furthermore, place pure water in new flasks and set them in the four intermediate directions.
According to one's means, prepare various kinds of food and offer them to the nāgas.
Furthermore, scatter fragrant flowers within the site of enlightenment (maṇḍala) and upon the Dharma seats in the four directions.
In each of the four directions, use pure, fresh cow-dung juice to draw the forms of nāgas.
To the east, three cubits beyond the seat,
draw the form of a dragon with one body and three heads, together with its retinue.
To the south, five cubits beyond the seat.
One should depict the form of a nāga with one body and five heads, together with its retinue,
seven cubits away from the seat toward the west;
and one should depict the form of a nāga with one body and seven heads, together with its retinue.
To the north, at a distance of nine cubits from the seat and beyond,
one should draw the form of a dragon with one body and nine heads, together with its retinue.
The mantra-reciter should protect himself.
Alternatively, one may consecrate pure water or white ash with mantras and,
while recollecting them in one's own mind, use them to demarcate the boundary of the site;
or one may draw a single step, or even many steps.
One may use water or ash to mark the boundary;
or one may tie a consecrated thread around the neck, the hand, or the foot;
and when consecrating the water or ash, one should sprinkle them upon the crown of the head.
If one should form this thought upon the forehead:
"Those with evil minds shall not enter this ritual boundary (maṇḍala)," then the reciter of the mantra shall give rise to compassion for all sentient beings.
I entreat all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to look upon us with compassion and grant their protection.
I dedicate this merit and share it with all the nāgas,
so that at times when there is no rain, [they may bring it].
If one recites this sutra for one day, two days, or even up to seven days without ceasing the sound,
then by the same method as above, rain will certainly fall.
Even the tides of the great ocean may be made to stay beyond their appointed time.
If one can fully possess these qualities and practice accordingly,
it is impossible for rain not to fall—
except in the case of those who lack faith and do not practice with a sincere heart.
The Mahāmegha Sūtra, Chapter Sixty-four: On Entreaty for Rain.
